To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) an elite suppressor developed de novo CD8 + T cell responses that suppressed replication by multiple HIV-1 escape mutants, and (2) the de novo CD8 T cell responses may contribute to the elite control of HIV-1 in this patient.

An HLA-B*5701 positive elite suppressor who developed seven rare escape variants at the Gag epitope 77-85 (SLYNTVATL) developed proliferative de novo CD8 T cell responses to each variant, which suppressed replication of each variant in vitro, suggesting that de novo CD8 responses may be important in elite control.
a single ES developed seven distinct escape mutants at a single epitope and that each mutant was suppressed by de novo, proliferative CTL responses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that allow some HIV-1 infected individuals to control HIV-1 replication in the absence of treatment.
how the immune system responds to viral variants and how these responses can be used to develop new therapies.
the study of HIV-1 and SIV pathogenesis and immunity in humans and non-human primates (NHP) using a combination of in vitro, ex vivo and in vivo approaches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ES developed a de novo response that controlled the viral variants.
the ES described in this study has been able to control HIV-1 replication by developing de novo CD8 T cell responses that suppress replication of multiple escape mutants.
the patient in this study developed multiple escape mutants at the same epitope, and the patient was able to suppress the replication of these mutants with de novo CD8 + T cell responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified an ES patient who developed multiple escape variants over the course of five years, and that these escape variants were suppressed by de novo CTL responses.
de novo CTL responses are capable of controlling rare escape mutants, even in the absence of a pre-existing response.
the immune system is able to suppress multiple escape variants, even if they are rare, and that the immune response is not necessarily directed at a single epitope.
The main takeaway from our work is that
elite control of HIV-1 is not due to a single immune mechanism.
the development of new CTL responses can suppress replication of rare variants in ES, and may be a mechanism by which ES maintain control.
de novo CD8 + T cell responses can be induced in ES patients, which may contribute to viral suppression of multiple escape variants in these patients.
